ddl:
CREATE TABLE Publication (
    Author VARCHAR(255),
    Price FLOAT,
    Publication_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Title VARCHAR(255),
    Type VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Customer (
    Customer_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Phone VARCHAR(255),
    Registration_Status VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Administrator (
    Administrator_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Phone VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Order (
    Customer_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Order_Status VARCHAR(255),
    Order_Time DATETIME,
    Payment_Method VARCHAR(255),
    Publication_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Shipping_Address VARCHAR(255),
    PRIMARY KEY (Customer_ID, Publication_ID, Order_Time),
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customer(Customer_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Publication_ID) REFERENCES Publication(Publication_ID)
);
gold_question: A publishing house plans to develop an online store, ACShop, for selling academic publications. The functional requirements are as follows: The online academic publications include papers, academic reports, and lecture materials. Publication information includes Publication ID, Title, Author, Price, and Type. Customer information includes Customer ID, Name, Phone, Email, Password, and Registration Status. ACShop will automatically generate orders, with order information including Publication ID, Customer ID, Shipping Address, Payment Method, Order Status, and Order Time. Administrators are responsible for maintaining the online publication catalog, including adding new publications or updating information on available publications. Administrator information includes Administrator ID, Name, Phone, Email, and Password.

The database schema named 'rschema_0473' contains four tables: 'Publication', 'Customer', 'Administrator', and 'Order'.
The 'Publication' table represents the published books and their details. It has columns for 'Author' (a string of up to 255 characters), 'Price' (a floating-point number), 'Publication_ID' (an integer primary key), 'Title' (a string of up to 255 characters), and 'Type' (a string of up to 255 characters).
The 'Customer' table represents the customers who can place orders. It has columns for 'Customer_ID' (an integer primary key), 'Email' (a string of up to 255 characters), 'Name' (a string of up to 255 characters), 'Password' (a string of up to 255 characters), 'Phone' (a string of up to 255 characters), and 'Registration_Status' (a string of up to 255 characters).
The 'Administrator' table represents the administrators who manage the system. It has columns for 'Administrator_ID' (an integer primary key), 'Email' (a string of up to 255 characters), 'Name' (a string of up to 255 characters), 'Password' (a string of up to 255 characters), and 'Phone' (a string of up to 255 characters).
The 'Order' table represents the orders placed by customers. It has columns for 'Customer_ID' (an integer that references 'Customer_ID' in the 'Customer' table), 'Order_Status' (a string of up to 255 characters), 'Order_Time' (a datetime), 'Payment_Method' (a string of up to 255 characters), 'Publication_ID' (an integer that references 'Publication_ID' in the 'Publication' table), and 'Shipping_Address' (a string of up to 255 characters). The primary key of this table is a composite of 'Customer_ID', 'Publication_ID', and 'Order_Time'. The 'Customer_ID' and 'Publication_ID' columns are foreign keys that reference the 'Customer' and 'Publication' tables respectively.
